business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Swiss Confederation; national-level reporting with cantonal administrative execution; registered office recommended in the Canton of Zug for e-commerce and private-banking alignment)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law — Swiss legal system based on the Swiss Civil Code (SR 210) and the Code of Obligations (SR 220), with cantonal procedural autonomy in commercial registration and notarial practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Switzerland Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 16 January 1986; amended by the Protocol of 27 April 2010)
China–Switzerland Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014)
China–Switzerland Double Taxation Agreement (signed 25 September 2013; in force 1 January 2015)
Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, as amended by the 2010 Protocol)
Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Hague Apostille Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 620 et seq. on the Aktiengesellschaft, including Art. 626 (articles of association), Art. 632-633 (minimum capital and paid-in capital), Art. 697l (company-level internal register of beneficial owners); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as revised; Financial Services Act (FinSA, SR 954.1) and Financial Institutions Act (FinIA, SR 954.1) to the extent applicable; FINMA Circular 2020/1 on anti-money laundering; Federal Act on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RwB) and its implementing Ordinance (RwBV), in force since 1 July 2023 (mandatory electronic disclosure of UBOs to the federal register at incorporation); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Art. 305bis and 305ter; Federal Act on the Use of Registered Office Addresses and the prevention of letterbox companies.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — The Swiss federal UBO register is not publicly accessible; access is granted to Swiss authorities (MROS Money Laundering Reporting Office, FINMA, prosecution authorities, tax and enforcement bodies) and to parties that credibly demonstrate a legal interest for singular disclosure under the RwB. The company must internally maintain and annually verify its own UBO list (Art. 697l CO). Nominee arrangements are lawful only if the nominee discloses the identity of the beneficial owner to the company and consents to UBO registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised public deed of incorporation and notarised Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal notary public in the registered-office canton
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarial act (no apostille required for documents executed in Switzerland; to be filed with the Commercial Register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address of each founding shareholder and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in the country of origin of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent foreign authority, followed by certified Swiss translation (or consular legalization at the Swiss representation for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / extract of criminal record register for each director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified translation into the official language of the canton of registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of the blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) evidencing the paid-up minimum capital of at least CHF 50,000
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Swiss bank or Swiss branch of a foreign bank accepting the capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Written bank confirmation issued in Switzerland (no apostille required); must carry the bank's official signature and, where requested by the notary, a stamp

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration (UBO Declaration) pursuant to the RwB, identifying all natural persons ultimately holding 25% or more of the shares, voting rights, or control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and directors, submitted through the formation fiduciary or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised signatures of the declarants; if signed outside Switzerland, each signature page requires Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised power of attorney appointing the Swiss formation agent / fiduciary to execute the incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholder (corporate or natural person) in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified translation into the canton's official register language (German, French, or Italian)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, directors, senior managers, shareholders, UBOs, and high-value consignors/sellers against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions ordinances and associated watchlists; (iii) the OFAC SDN list and sectoral sanctions administered by the US Department of the Treasury; (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) classifications consistent with FATF Recommendations and FINMA Circular 2020/1, including family members and close associates. Screening must occur prior to onboarding and at least quarterly thereafter, with enhanced due diligence applied to: cross-border luxury consignments with unit value above CHF 25,000, cash-derived proceeds, jurisdictions appearing on FATF high-risk lists, and any legal person using nominee or bearer share structures. For the target entity's payment rails (Stripe, Escrow_Pay), the Swiss acquiring bank and payment service provider will apply their own OFAC/UN/SECO screening, and the company must contractually require that enhanced due diligence be performed on every seller and buyer where the transaction value triggers AMLA thresholds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix — Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Commercial Register (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office; formal preliminary name checks ('Abklärung') and incorporation filings are made through the competent cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt) via a Swiss notary in the canton of the registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin script characters, whether in a Swiss national language (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) or in a foreign-language designation readable in the Latin alphabet, subject always to the principle of truthfulness under Art. 950 para. 2 of the Code of Obligations. The mandatory legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' must be appended. The name must not be misleading, deceptive, capable of confusing the public, or contrary to public policy, and must not reproduce a prior-registered name or a trademark protected in Switzerland. English trade names are permissible as secondary names provided the registered statutory name remains in an accepted script and format.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Helvetia (where used in a manner suggesting state affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial name-clearance window of 30 days may not be extended as a matter of right; upon expiry the applicant must file a fresh preliminary name-check request, which opens a further 30-day window. Where the commercial registrar rejects the requested name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal within 30 days pursuant to Art. 44 et seq. of the Federal Act on Administrative Procedure (SR 172.021), addressed to the competent cantonal supervisory authority over the commercial register. An adverse decision of the cantonal supervisory authority may be further appealed to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of notification. Concurrently, and without prejudice to the appeal, the applicant may submit a revised company name for a new clearance process so as not to delay the incorporation timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — The Canton of Zug and other cantons permit the use of a licensed professional domiciliation provider (fiduciary) at a physical commercial address, provided the company maintains access to its corporate records, statutory books, and official correspondence and performs its administrative seat in substance at that address. A pure virtual letterbox address or mail-forwarding-only service is not compliant with the Swiss registered-office address legislation and the anti-letterbox-company jurisprudence. For a cross-border e-commerce and vintage-luxury consignment business, the statutory seat may be at a professional domicile provider, but the company must evidence commercial substance through physical or contracted third-party warehousing, logistics, insurance, and bookkeeping arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 60% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 36 months of operation, rising to approximately 75% where the registered office is maintained exclusively at a professional domiciliation address without separate operational premises. Inspection triggers include the Swiss commercial register offices, cantonal fiscal authorities (for VAT registration above CHF 100,000 turnover), SECO sanctions monitoring, and due-diligence visits by the acquiring bank or escrow payment partner.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Paid-in minimum share capital deposit under Art. 632 and Art. 633 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (blocked account / Sperrkonto)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss bank holding the blocked capital account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement of CHF 100,000 nominal, of which at least CHF 50,000 (approx. USD 58,000) must be paid in cash at incorporation; refundable to the company upon completion of registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of the public deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary public in the registered-office canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff; prevailing market benchmark CHF 1,500-2,500 for an Aktiengesellschaft incorporation deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register registration fee for the formation of an Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official tariff under the Swiss Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (SR 221.411), base CHF 600 plus additional CHF 50-200 per entry and per authorised signatory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO beneficial-owner notification to the federal register (RwB) as part of the incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office / Federal Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal official fee for the simultaneous statutory filing of the beneficial-owner declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary company name clearance ('Abklärung') with the cantonal registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal official fee for formal pre-registration name verification per candidate name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Zefix/Commercial Register extracts, company seal, corporate share certificates, and statutory corporate records kit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Register Office and corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory extract fees and prevailing market benchmark for the initial corporate documentation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal VAT and UID number registration (Swiss Value Added Tax Act, SR 641.20)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration free of charge; mandatory for e-commerce activity once annual taxable turnover reaches CHF 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formation legal counsel and AML/CFT, UBO, and sanctions compliance advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss law firm or licensed fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CHF 250-450 per hour; fixed-fee engagement CHF 2,500-5,000 for AG establishment with cross-border component

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of constitutive documents into the official language of the canton of registration (German, French, or Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of approximately CHF 150-300 per hour per document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of four to six foreign-origin documents (passports, good conduct certificates, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authority (Ministry of Foreign Affairs / consulate of the country of origin)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document official fee of USD 200-350 plus courier and consular handling charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and blocked capital confirmation (Sperrkonto certificate) at a Swiss private bank or neobank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank account opening fee of CHF 150-400, sometimes waived for private-banking clients with onboarding asset volume

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal, share register, and statutory records binder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate supplies and record-keeping initialization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office / domiciliation service at a licensed fiduciary provider for the first twelve months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation or fiduciary provider in the canton of registered office (recommended: Zug or Zurich)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual domiciliation fee of CHF 1,500-3,000 for an Aktiengesellschaft with professional mail handling and compliance support

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Articles 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / societe anonyme); Swiss Civil Code (ZGB, SR 210) Articles 52 ff.; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt Zug), with appellate oversight of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenossisches Handelsregisteramt / Office federal du registre du commerce, Bern).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde / acte de constitution) together with the Articles of Incorporation (Statuten / statuts); filed through the eGRIS electronic register platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG requires minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (CO Art. 621). At incorporation, at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid in cash, but in no event less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate, before registration (CO Art. 632). The funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a licensed Swiss bank in the company's name; the bank issues a payment confirmation and the board retains no unrestricted right of disposal until registration. Contributions in kind (Sacheinlage) require a special audit report and disclosure in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: APPROVED, the Articles of Association of the Company, as notarized, are hereby ratified, together with the subscription of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100.00 nominal value each, constituting an aggregate share capital of CHF 100,000. APPROVED, the registered office is established at [street, city, canton], Switzerland. APPROVED, the capital contribution account held by [bank] is recognized; management is instructed to maintain the restriction on disposal until commercial registration. APPROVED, [name] is appointed chairman of the board and sole director with individual signature authority, and [name] is appointed authorized signatory. APPROVED, [audit firm] is appointed statutory auditor, subject to the auditor waiver. APPROVED, the directors shall effect all commercial register filings and tax notifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public admitted in the canton of the registered office (e.g., Notariat Zug / Notary Public of Zurich)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders must appear before a cantonal notary for authentication of the deed of incorporation and articles. Provide valid passports or Swiss identity documents; the notary verifies legal capacity, reads the articles aloud, and notarizes the statutory declaration. The articles must contain the corporate name, registered office address, purpose, share capital of at least CHF 100,000 divided into registered shares, par value, board composition, auditors, and publication provisions. If any contribution in kind is made, an audit report under CO Art. 635a and a report on pre-incorporation transactions must be attached.
required_dossiers: Passport or Swiss identity document of each founder
Draft Articles of Association with entity name and purpose
Draft notarial deed of incorporation
Declaration of legal representatives and authorized signatories
Report of the statutory auditor on any contribution in kind if non-cash assets are transferred
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to non-compliant clauses (CO Art. 626-640), amend the statutes to conform and execute a fresh notarial session; any defect in the purpose or capital clause is cured by filing revised articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment-in of minimum share capital and bank confirmation of escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or securities dealer (e.g., UBS Switzerland AG, Zuger Kantonalbank) and, where non-cash contributions are used, a licensed audit firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate share capital escrow account in the name of the company being formed. Each founder transfers his or her contribution in cash or bank-cleared funds to the account. The bank issues a capital payment confirmation (Bestätigung der Einzahlung) that the paid-in amount reaches at least CHF 50,000, being 20% of the CHF 100,000 nominal value. The account must remain blocked so that neither the board nor the founders can dispose of funds until the Commercial Register entry is completed and the capital is shown as paid in under CO Art. 632.
required_dossiers: Bank capital payment confirmation letter
Founders' payment receipts or credit slips
Audit expert report on non-cash valuation if a Sacheinlage is used
List of share subscriptions and allotments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses confirmation because of incomplete deposits, require each subscriber to pay the outstanding fraction within five banking days; if the audit expert revises an asset valuation downwards, increase the cash portion accordingly through a supplementary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for incorporation with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the canton of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt Zug / Zurich), in coordination with the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA / OFRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application through the eGRIS electronic register platform or at the competent cantonal registry counter. The registry checks the formal legality of the deed, the statutes, the bank capital confirmation, and the residence and signature rights of board members; at least one director must be resident in Switzerland with individual signature authority (CO Art. 708). Upon approval, the entry is published in the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB); the company acquires legal personality upon entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Articles of Association
Bank capital payment confirmation
Declaration of directors accepting appointment, with signature card and specimen signatures
Declaration by shareholders on residency and beneficial ownership (GwG / AML)
Written consent of the landlord to the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a query (Zwischenverfügung) by the Register Office, submit written responses and corrective evidence within the prescribed time limit, usually 10 days, or request an extension; amend the statutes if required, re-notarize the amended pages, and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Acquisition of legal personality and mandatory tax, VAT and social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC Bern), cantonal tax administration, cantonal AHV compensation office (Ausgleichskasse), and SUVA accident insurance fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after the Commercial Register entry, the newly formed AG must apply for a Swiss Business Identification Number (UID) through the central UID portal, register for VAT if turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year, file the corporate tax questionnaire with the cantonal tax administration, and register as an employer with the compensation fund (AHV/IV/EO/ALV) and with SUVA for occupational accident insurance. The company must also notify the local municipality (Gemeinde) of its business activity.
required_dossiers: Handelsregisterauszug (commercial register excerpt)
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
UID registration form submitted via eServices
Cantonal corporate tax questionnaire
Employer registration declarations for AHV and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a late registration penalty is threatened, file an immediate written application referring to the date of legal formation, attach the register excerpt, and request remission or limitation of the penalty; for VAT, retroactive registration is admissible upon proof of economic activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises admission: fire safety certification, structural occupancy clearance and occupational health registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal building and fire inspectorate, cantonal building insurance company (e.g., Gebäudeversicherung Zug), and the municipal or cantonal labour inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the rented office and high-value goods warehouse of the vintage luxury resale business, submit the tenancy lease and floor plan; obtain confirmation that the fire protection concept (evacuation routes, extinguishers, emergency lighting) satisfies cantonal fire police standards (VKF / AEAI). The structural engineer or building authority must certify floor-loading capacity for storage racks. Register the workplace with the canton, carry out a risk assessment under the Labour Act (ArG) and the Accident Prevention Ordinance (VUV), and notify SUVA of the employee accident insurance.
required_dossiers: Rental leases for the registered office and warehouse
Floor plans with fire protection design
Evidence of fire extinguishing equipment and emergency exits
Structural load certification of racking areas
Workplace risk assessment report
Occupational health and safety self-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspectorate refuses the occupancy permit, execute the required retrofits (fire doors, signage, extinguishers) within the cure period and request re-inspection; arrange alternative compliant warehousing during the cure period if temporary use is prohibited.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal trade supervision office (Gewerbeamt / Office du commerce) and the cantonal labour inspectorate, under the supervisory framework of the Federal Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO); no federal sectoral licence is required for online second-hand luxury goods retail.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business activity notification (Betriebsanzeige / declaration d'activite) and premises occupancy permit (Nutzungsbewilligung) for the e-commerce office and warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) and the cantonal environmental protection agency (Amt für Umweltschutz) of the registered office canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Exempt from full EIA (UVP-Pflicht): an e-commerce warehouse under 6,000 m2 usable floor area does not trigger the annex thresholds of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OEIE); only simplified environmental registration with the canton is required for waste handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant process wastewater or VOC emissions arise from consignment warehousing; comply with the Federal Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) discharge prohibitions, the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) Art. 4 emission limits, the Noise Protection Ordinance (LSV), and the Packaging Ordinance (VAV) packaging recovery duty; returned or defective luxury goods must be handled through licensed recycling and waste operators under the Ordinance on Waste Movements (VeVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the cantonal fire police and Gebaeudeversicherung in accordance with VKF / AEAI standards; structural load inspection confirming floor capacity for high-value storage racks; emergency escape and extinguisher scheme; civil defense obligations under cantonal civil protection legislation; and occupational health and safety clearance under the Labour Act (ArG), including SUVA employer registration and mandatory accident insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), official portal www.estv.admin.ch, with the e-service portal 'MeinSwissVAT' (https://mein.swissvat.ch) for VAT registration, filing and refunds; federal/communal tax administration of the cantonal seat applies for direct taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG automatically obtains its UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / Identificateur d'entreprise / Identificatore d'impresa, format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) upon entry in the cantonal commercial register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce / Registro di commercio) and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB/FOSC/FUSC); the UID, issued by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, serves as the statutory TIN and as the VAT identification number once VAT registration is approved. VAT registration is filed with the ESTV via MeinSwissVAT using Form 'Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuer' accompanied by the articles of incorporation, commercial register excerpt and turnover projections; foreign entities without a Swiss registered seat must demonstrate Swiss taxable nexus and may be required to appoint a Swiss fiscal representative before the ESTV grants a CHE UID/VAT number, with processing typically completed within 15 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box elections. Available mechanisms include: (i) the participation exemption (Beteiligungsabzug / déduction pour participation) automatically applied on the tax return for qualifying dividends and capital gains (minimum 10% or CHF 1 million fair value participation held for 12 months); (ii) notional interest deduction (NID) elections in certain cantons (e.g., Zurich, Geneva); (iii) VAT group election (Mehrwertsteuer-Gruppenbesteuerung) integrating closely held Swiss entities as one VAT taxpayer; (iv) advance tax rulings (Steuervorbescheid / ruling) with the cantonal tax administration and ESTV for hybrid financing and cross-border structures; (v) transitional privileged statuses (holding, domicile, auxiliary companies) which are being phased out from 2025 for multinational groups in scope of the Swiss Minimum Tax Act implementing the OECD Global Minimum Tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Mehrwertsteuer (MWST) / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) / Imposta sul valore aggiunto (IVA), governed by the Swiss VAT Act (MWSTG/LTVA/LIVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding VAT) in the preceding business year; no de minimis relief for foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Switzerland, except where the Swiss recipient applies the reverse-charge mechanism; small Swiss businesses below CHF 100,000 may elect voluntary VAT registration; foreign e-commerce operators selling goods into Switzerland to private consumers are registrable regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-authorisation or digital stamping regime exists in Switzerland. E-invoices are valid provided authenticity of origin and integrity of content are preserved via recognised electronic transmission, qualified electronic signature, or EDI/secure interchange agreement; Swiss QR-bill and eBill formats are accepted. From 1 January 2026, suppliers to the Swiss federal administration must transmit structured e-invoices through the SwissPeppol/Peppol network. VAT returns are filed quarterly or semi-annually through MeinSwissVAT; payment is due within 60 days of the reporting period. No continuous transaction-control (CTC) API obligation applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies to goods physically exported from Switzerland to foreign territories when the AG proves that the goods left Swiss customs territory as a result of the supply; the supplier must be the exporter of record and the goods must be transported abroad. Services directly related to exported movable goods, freight forwarding, storage, and intermediary services supplied to foreign principals are zero-rated or fall outside Swiss VAT scope under the B2B reverse-charge principle. For online vintage luxury resale, the 0% rate requires physical shipment from Switzerland to the foreign customer's destination; supplies fulfilled from a foreign warehouse (third-party fulfilment) are not zero-rated and may create destination-country VAT obligations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e-dec / SafeBorder) bearing the export registration number (Zollanmeldung / déclaration d'exportation / dichiarazione di esportazione)
Transport document — Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR/CIM consignment note evidencing departure from Switzerland and arrival at the foreign destination
Commercial invoice, online sales order or consignment contract and, where applicable, the vintage luxury authentication certificate establishing the secondhand good's provenance and value
Proof of payment / inward remittance certificate (SWIFT bank confirmation, Stripe settlement report or Escrow disbursement record) showing receipt from the foreign buyer
Carrier logistics report with tracking events and signed delivery acknowledgement for low-value parcel consignments
Insurance certificate and/or certificate of origin for high-value luxury items as value-supporting evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT law requires the taxpayer to retain zero-rating evidence in business records; insufficient export substantiation triggers VAT reassessment at 8.1%, default interest at 4.5% p.a. (5% as from 1 January 2025) and potential administrative fines up to CHF 800,000 for intentional tax evasion under Art. 100 MWSTG. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute tax fraud under Art. 101 MWSTG, sanctionable by imprisonment up to 3 years or monetary penalty, plus retrospective clawbacks with a 10-year assessment period in cases of intent. Although Swiss exchange-control rules do not impose a statutory 180-day FX-repatriation deadline, inward remittance within 180 days is the documentary benchmark accepted by the ESTV on audit for cross-border e-commerce; missing or contradictory payment evidence invites full risk-based audits, retroactive VAT clawbacks and publication of penalty decisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) in conjunction with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF); foreign exchange administration is liberalized under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA), with prudential supervision by FINMA and sanctions enforcement by SECO.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc for both current and capital account transactions. There is no general foreign exchange control law, no exchange licensing regime, and no restriction on dividend distributions, loan repatriation, or liquidation proceeds for domestic Aktiengesellschaften. Profit remittance is subject only to Swiss corporate income taxation and the 35% withholding tax on dividends, which may be reduced under an applicable double tax treaty. Bank transfers in CHF, EUR, USD, and other major currencies are freely permitted, subject to AML/KYC screening, sanctions screening, and counterparty due diligence by the receiving or instructing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline. Exporters of vintage luxury goods, including online consignment resellers, may retain foreign currency proceeds in Swiss bank accounts or in accounts abroad without obligation to convert into CHF. The only constraints arise from sanctions, FINMA circulars on liquidity management, and internal bank policy on foreign-currency position limits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability for offshore fintech EMI and digital banking providers. They may serve as complementary payment collection rails for Stripe, PayPal, and Escrow Pay settlement, but they cannot act as the primary treasury account for capital escrow verification under Swiss company law (CO Art. 634). A FINMA-licensed or FINMA-recognized Swiss bank must hold the registered share capital. Offshore EMIs are generally permissive as multi-currency operational conduits, but they trigger enhanced AML review, may lack direct SIC/SIC4 access, and are not suitable for large-value CHF clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, FINMA-regulated banks require at least one director, the ultimate beneficial owner, or a duly authorized representative with power of attorney to appear physically for the KYC interview. Fully remote onboarding is rare and is granted only for low-risk structures with a strong Swiss nexus, not for cross-border vintage luxury e-commerce. Enhanced due-diligence procedures under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and FINMA Circular 2016/7 require personal identification, verification of commercial purpose, and confirmation of source of funds. Video-identification can be used only where the bank operates an accredited onboarding channel and the corporate structure is simple.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk classification due to online marketplace activity, cross-border payment aggregation, and the secondhand luxury goods sector (ISIC 4791).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association; certified extract from the Swiss commercial register; board resolution establishing signatory authority; complete ultimate beneficial ownership chart; notarized passports of all directors and UBOs; detailed business plan; marketplace platform contracts (Stripe, Escrow Pay); domain and trademark registration; source-of-wealth documentation; opening balance sheet or audited financial statements; compliance manual and AML policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented inbound customer payments and correspondingly fragmented outbound seller disbursements indicating possible money laundering or commingling of client funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement with full reconciliation methodology; auditable ERP or accounting ledger mapping buyer funds to seller payouts; monthly payment processor settlement reports; payout reports from Stripe/Escrow Pay; bank statements; anti-money-laundering internal controls; dedicated client-money policy; compliance officer appointment letter; training logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows involving high-risk jurisdictions, unusual provenance, or vintage luxury goods prone to trade-based money laundering and invoice manipulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete provenance chain for luxury items: purchase invoices, authentication and appraisal certificates, condition reports, consignment contracts, certificates of origin; HS codes and Swiss-specific import/export documentation; sanctions and denied-party screening logs; SECO export confirmation where applicable; transport and customs documents; payment/beneficiary due-diligence files; independent valuation reports for high-value items.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital contributions are made through ordinary SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer to the Swiss capital escrow account. The CHF contribution of at least CHF 100,000 must be irrevocably received and at the free disposal of the board before registration. Remittance information must identify the purpose as 'Share capital contribution under Art. 632 and 633 CO' and reference the company name. Foreign exchange controls do not apply, but the operating bank will require proof of the ultimate originator, a capital release declaration, and confirmation that the funds are not of criminal origin. Beneficiary account should be at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank; no prior exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments use SWIFT MT103 standard clearing rails for CHF, EUR, USD, and GBP. CHF payments are cleared through SIC/SIC4 real-time gross settlement; EUR through SEPA and Target2; USD through the bank's US correspondent and Fedwire/CHIPS. Commercial letters of credit are available via UBS or ZKB when transacting with auction houses and institutional consignors. All outbound disbursements require underlying contract documentation, commercial invoice, and sanctions screening. For buyer-seller escrow flows, funds are held on Escrow Pay and released through SEPA or SWIFT to verified seller bank accounts upon condition satisfaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards in CHF/EUR and CHF/USD with Swiss or EU/UK banking counterparties under established ISDA/CSA documentation.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing multi-currency treasury liquidity, including the conversion of EUR/USD sales proceeds into CHF operating cash flow.
European-style vanilla FX options to hedge transaction exposure from auction purchases and overseas inventory replenishment.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted in uncommon or restricted-convertibility currencies, but are generally unnecessary for CHF, EUR, or USD and must be handled by a licensed derivatives broker under the Swiss Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FinMIA).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement and notes) presented for approval at the annual general meeting and submitted to the cantonal tax authority in support of the corporate income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Annual General Meeting of shareholders; Cantonal Tax Administration (e.g., Zug Steuerverwaltung) as annexure to the tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting must be held and annual accounts approved within six months of the balance sheet date; calendar-year company: by 30 June (OR Art. 699 para. 1).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' liability for breach of convening duties; court-ordered audit at shareholder application (OR Art. 730a); tax assessments based on estimated profits with default interest at 5% per annum when accounts are not provided.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return comprising Federal Direct Tax, cantonal income tax and capital tax, including signed financial statements and required schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (principal filing office, e.g., Zug); Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for the federal direct tax portion.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; standard extended deadline of 30 June where the return is prepared by a licensed Swiss tax advisor; further extension on justified request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and default interest at 5% per annum; administrative fine of up to 30% of evaded tax for incorrect or incomplete declarations; criminal tax evasion proceedings and director/officer personal liability in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (quarterly reporting period, or annual return where annual reporting has been granted) for taxable turnover generated by the online luxury resale platform.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Swiss Value Added Tax Division.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly returns due within 60 days after the end of each quarter; annual returns due within 60 days after the end of the business year (calendar-year VAT return by approximately 1 March).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum; administrative fine up to 30% of the tax evaded; collection reminder procedures and risk of suspension of the VAT number and loss of input VAT deduction rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent auditor's report (review report for simplified audit or full audit report for ordinary audit) covering the annual financial statements and submitted to the annual general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent Swiss-certified audit firm; report presented to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting and retained with the annual accounts (not filed with the Commercial Register).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be issued before the Annual General Meeting; meeting must be held within six months of the balance sheet date (calendar-year company: report by 30 June).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Dividend distributions and profit appropriations are unlawful without the required audit (OR Art. 660a/858); court appointment of a special auditor (OR Art. 697b); civil liability of directors and auditors for false statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit (OR Art. 727): required where the company exceeds any two of the following in two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, average workforce above 250 full-time employees; also mandatory for companies with more than 500 full-time employees or listed/regulated entities. Simplified audit (review; OR Art. 727a): required where the company exceeds any two of the following in two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 10 million, turnover above CHF 2 million, average workforce above 10 full-time employees. Opt-out (unanimous shareholder consent) is available only where the simplified-audit thresholds are not exceeded for two consecutive financial years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (OR Art. 957-963b), applied as Swiss statutory GAAP; Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS used for consolidated reporting and increasingly adopted for statutory accounts; IFRS mandatory for listed groups. Business books, vouchers and annual accounts must be retained for 10 years (OR Art. 958f).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not currently impose an annual UBO confirmation filing to the Commercial Register. The Aktiengesellschaft must maintain the Aktienbuch (share register) recording all registered shareholders (OR Art. 685i-r) and must record the beneficial owners of any bearer shares (OR Art. 697k). Banks and payment service providers (e.g., Stripe, Escrow-Pay) require annual UBO self-certification and KYC refresh under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act. A central UBO register with additional annual confirmation obligations is pending under draft Swiss transparency legislation and is not yet in force.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per year (CHF 1,000 - 3,000) for domiciliation and registered-office services at a Swiss commercial hub (Zug/Zurich), including corporate housekeeping and commercial register notifications.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 12,000 per year for a simplified audit (review) of a small-to-medium Aktiengesellschaft; USD 12,000 - 30,000 per year for an ordinary statutory audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss federal corporate income tax is levied at a headline statutory rate of 8.5% on after-tax profit, equivalent to approximately 4.26% on a pre-tax basis because the federal and cantonal corporate income taxes are deductible in determining taxable profit. Combined effective rates including cantonal and communal taxes generally range from approximately 12% to 21% depending on the tax domicile; a Zug-domiciled AG is commonly around 14.5% while a Zurich-domiciled AG can reach approximately 21%. No general statutory tax holidays exist. Relevant preferential deductions include the participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains, the Swiss patent box regime allowing preferential taxation of qualifying IP income, and optional R&D super deductions permitted by cantonal law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal legal-entity tax return for Aktiengesellschaften, designated as the 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' or 'Tax Return for Legal Entities', filed through the cantonal tax administration's electronic portal. The return simultaneously governs the federal direct tax, cantonal and communal income tax, and capital tax assessment; ancillary federal filings such as VAT and withholding-tax matters are separately submitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), and Country-by-Country Reporting notifications are submitted through the ESTV e-portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The return covers one full financial year; if the financial year ends on a date other than 31 December, the annual return follows that balance-sheet date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year AG the normal deadline is 30 June of the following year. Written extension requests filed with the cantonal tax authority may extend this period, typically to 30 September or later, but extension is not automatic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal form (AG), registered commercial registry number, registered office, share capital, and principal purpose.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders must not be listed as Swiss resident taxpayers; a foreign parent company's address is disclosed only if a permanent establishment or Swiss real property is held.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial income statement reconciliation: annual book profit or loss per audited or approved financial statements, including extraordinary and non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income allocable to the Swiss AG or to its Swiss permanent establishment; foreign-source operating income is reported in full unless a relevant tax treaty allocation changes the Swiss attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: gifts, excessive board or director compensation, expenses for evasion-relevant purposes, bribery payments, partially non-deductible entertainment, and expenses relating to non-arm's-length dealings with related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid by the Swiss AG to non-resident related parties for services, royalties, or group charges must be backed by service contracts, actual performance, and arm's-length pricing; otherwise add back and reclassify as constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of Swiss federal and cantonal/communal corporate income taxes and withholding taxes already expensed in prior periods, to the extent legally deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes borne on outbound dividends are not deductible at Swiss entity level unless the shares are held as Swiss business assets and a corresponding expense is recognized in the commercial books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption: deduction of qualifying dividends and capital gains derived from a shareholding of at least 10% held for a minimum period of one financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder cannot claim the participation exemption in the Swiss AG return; the exemption belongs to the Swiss holding company and applies to qualifying domestic and foreign participations in the AG's own books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset: deduction of available tax losses carried forward from prior years, subject to the seven-year carryforward limit and legal requirements on maintenance of accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss AG with a non-resident shareholder may offset only its own Swiss tax losses; losses of foreign shareholders or affiliated foreign companies are not transferable to the AG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable profit: adjusted commercial profit after add-backs and deductions, then apportioned between federal and cantonal/communal jurisdictions as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the AG has a permanent establishment outside Switzerland, profits attributable to that foreign PE are exempt in Switzerland under the applicable DTA provided the PE income is honestly allocated and documented; a mere foreign bank account or escrow account does not create a PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a valid extension triggers a cantonal procedural fine typically up to CHF 10,000, plus default interest at a rate generally between 4% and 5% per annum on resulting additional taxes. If the taxpayer continues to refuse filing, the cantonal tax authority may assess by estimation, deny deductions, and escalate the case to tax-evasion proceedings carrying fines up to the amount of tax evaded, with additional interest. Repeated violations can lead to registration of the taxpayer in the cantonal enforcement register.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Swiss federal withholding tax is levied at 35% on gross dividends paid by the Swiss AG to all beneficial owners, including non-residents. Treaty relief is not automatic at source. The non-resident beneficial owner must file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, using a withholding-tax refund request and attaching a valid tax residence certificate issued by the foreign tax administration, together with evidence of beneficial ownership and holding period as required under the specific Swiss DTA and the Multilateral Instrument. Refund claims generally must be filed within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. Relief-at-source clearance may be granted only where the foreign financial intermediary or custodian has an approved Swiss procedure and the treaty relief has been pre-certified by ESTV.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Swiss law imposes no withholding tax on royalties, so the statutory rate is 0%, and most Swiss income tax treaties allocate royalty taxing rights to the residence state. Swiss withholding tax at 35% applies to interest paid on Swiss bond-like obligations, money-market instruments, and certain bank deposit/book-account interest; ordinary intercompany loans that are not securitised into a Swiss bond or bill are generally outside WHT. Treaty rates on interest vary from 0% to 10% depending on the treaty partner; in absence of treaty relief, the 35% rate applies to taxable Swiss interest instruments and the payor has a statutory duty to deduct.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate_comment: The 35% rate is the unified Swiss federal withholding tax rate; cantons do not impose an additional dividend withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law does not prescribe a fixed de minimis threshold for mandatory Local File or Master File filing. However, Switzerland applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines as interpretive authority and requires taxpayers to maintain and produce arm's-length documentation when requested by the tax administration. A Swiss constituent entity of a group with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more is subject to Country-by-Country Reporting: Swiss constituent entities of the group must file a CbC notification with the ESTV, and the ultimate parent entity, if Swiss resident, must file the full CbC report. In audit practice, material cross-border related-party transactions of any size — particularly vintage luxury resale stock purchased from or sold to related persons — must be robustly documented.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a statutory Economic Substance Regulations regime analogous to the EU or Caribbean ESR systems. Nevertheless, economic substance is essential for Swiss corporate residence, treaty entitlement, participation exemption, or withholding-tax relief. An AG whose board of directors, corporate records, business premises, bank accounts, and actual decision-making are demonstrably present in Switzerland is treated as a Swiss tax resident. A 'letter-box' AG directing the e-commerce luxury resale business from abroad will be re-characterised as managed from abroad; its Swiss residence may be denied, its foreign-related advantages revoked, and its intra-group payments reclassified as constructive dividends or hidden profit distributions subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Income tax evasion and false documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of online vintage luxury resale revenue, falsification of Stripe or escrow payment records, destruction of purchase invoices, issuance of counterfeit authentication certificates, concealment of sales proceeds in private digital wallets, and failure to report commissions paid to non-resident influencers or consignees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of omitted profit plus default interest; administrative tax-evasion penalty generally equal to the tax evaded and up to three times that amount where aggravated, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud under the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Taxation with imprisonment and fines. VAT evasion additionally triggers penalties and forfeiture of unlawfully avoided VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable under Swiss debt-enforcement law for wilful depletion of corporate assets during tax-enforcement proceedings; fraudulent concealment or falsification can result in criminal fines, imprisonment, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and extradition requests for international cooperation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Swiss AG is operated solely from a foreign domicile with no employees, premises, independent board activity, or de facto management in Switzerland; all commercial decisions for the luxury resale operation are centered abroad, while the AG claims Swiss residence, DTA relief, participation exemption, and payment-processing contracts with Stripe or Escrow_Pay from its Swiss letterbox.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of Swiss tax residence or re-attribution of taxable profits to the place of effective management; denial of treaty benefits and participation exemption; hidden distributions recharacterized and subjected to 35% WHT plus interest; closure of the company under commercial-registry procedure where the registered office no longer corresponds to substance; fines and sanctions for circuitous arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face joint and several liability under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 754 for damage caused by the sham construction, including restitution of tax advantages with interest, civil claims by creditors, disqualification from board service, travel bans in criminal proceedings, and potential confiscation of personal benefits obtained from the shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sales of secondhand luxury handbags to a foreign related reseller at cost, discount, or without comparability analysis; payment of excessive 'marketing promotion fees' to non-resident shareholders or influencers not rendering genuine services; unmatched TNMM margins; zero benchmark documentation for cross-border inventory purchase and inventory holding arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment by the Swiss tax administration, disallowance of the excessive expense, reclassification of the difference as a constructive dividend, 35% withholding tax plus default interest, and administrative fine for insufficient or false documents; taxpayer may also face contested assessment through the Swiss Federal Administrative Court if documentation remains inadequate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise non-arm's-length cross-border agreements can be held personally liable for resulting unpaid Swiss taxes if they knowingly exposed the company to tax fraud; veil piercing is available where the AG is used as a mere alter ego to drain profits overseas. Civil damages can include retroactive restitution of tax, interest, and procedural costs, and travel bans can be ordered where criminal charges for fiscal avoidance are investigated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/escrow compliance failures and payment-rail abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using payment rails such as Stripe and Escrow_Pay while failing to apply customer due diligence, beneficial-owner verification, or transaction monitoring; accepting large structured payments from unknown consignors; using escrow accounts to obscure the ultimate seller or beneficial owner of consigned luxury goods; facilitating the laundering of proceeds through the resale of high-value vintage goods without retention of transactional records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the AG acts as a financial intermediary or is otherwise subject to Swiss AMLA, violations attract regulatory sanctions, fines, and closure orders; money laundering under the Swiss Criminal Code is punishable by imprisonment and a fine, and the underlying assets — including luxury goods held for resale — are subject to confiscation. Sectoral licensing may be required if escrow activity is construed as financial intermediation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in or tolerating money-laundering structures may be personally prosecuted for money laundering or lack of due diligence, resulting in imprisonment, discovery of personal bank accounts and travel bans, asset freezing, disqualification and civil restitution of profits received; directors may also be ordered to repay the company for fines, penalties, and legal defence costs arising from their breach of duty.
